THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:37693  MFA No. 11352 of 2012  JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the insurance company aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.823/2011, dated 03.08.2012.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the claimant is that on 10.04.2010 at about 8.30 p.m., the deceased was crossing the Magadi-Bengaluru Main Road near Machohalli Gate at that time rider of motorcycle came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.

As a result, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was taken to Pooja Hospital, Machohalli and later shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bangalore for treatment, where he was treated as in-patient and later he succumbed to the injuries on 24.07.2010.

sentences.text: The court below considering the Police records, the IMV report and the charge-sheet had held that the NC: 2023:KHC:37693 accident had occurred because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the motorcycle and since it was insured with the insurance company, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and granted compensation of an amount of Rs.2,36,000/-.
Aggrieved by the same, now the insurance company is before this Court.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that though the claimant had failed to establish that the accident had taken place because of the negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler and without there being any positive evidence on record the court below had fastened the liability on the insurance company.
It is submitted that the accident had taken place on 10.04.2010 and the complaint was alleged to have been given on 14.04.2010.
Learned counsel submits that on a perusal of Exhibit-P1, complaint discloses that the same given without mentioning the date.

He submits that the said fact itself shows that there was any amount of NC:
2023:KHC:37693 doubt whether the said complaint was given on 14.04.2010.

Further, he submits that there are no eye witnesses to the accident and none were examined and that the accident had taken place while the deceased was crossing the road and there is negligence on his part.
That aspect was not considered.
Further it is submitted that in the MLC register except mentioning about the road traffic accident the number of the offending vehicle is not mentioned.
According to the learned counsel for the purpose of claiming the compensation the said vehicle is implicated in this case.
It is submitted that as per the post-mortem report the deceased died because of the respiratory failure which has nothing to do with the injuries sustained by him.
He submits that there is no nexus between the injuries and the death.
In view of the same insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation but still the trial court without appreciating this fact has fastened the liability on the insurance company.

Yesterday when the matter was listed as there was no representation on behalf of the respondents - claimants, this Court having heard the learned counsel for the appeal for giving an opportunity to the respondents - claimants had directed the matter to be listed today under the caption 'For Judgment'.
Today also there is no representation.
As this is an appeal of the year 2012 this court is not inclined to adjourn the matter and is proceeding to decide the same basing on the available material on the record.
6. Having heard the Learned counsel for two Insurance companies, perused the entire material on record.

In this case the accident had taken place on 14.04.2010 wherein according to the claimants when the deceased was crossing the main road the rider of the motorcycle came in a high speed and dashed the deceased immediately the extract of MLC Register was not filed by the claimant.
However the same is filed on behalf of the respondent and marked as Exhibit R-3.
As per the same NC: 2023:KHC:37693 the claimant was admitted in the hospital on 10.04.2010 at 9.30 p.m and the accident had occurred at 8.30 p.m.

, in the MLC extract it is mentioned that there was a road traffic accident near Machohalli Gate and the patient suffered swelling over left eye ball, and type-I compound comminuted fracture mid shaft bones of left leg.

sentences.text: On behalf of the claimant PW-1 and PW-2 were examined.
PW-1 is none other than the son of the deceased.
PW-2 is the Doctor who has treated the deceased.

The Doctor had deposed that the deceased who was aged about 78 years came to Victory Hospital on 10.04.2010 with a history of road traffic accident and sustained type-I compound comminuted fracture mid shaft both bones of left leg and during his treatment surgery of open reduction and internal fixation with implants was done.
According to the Doctor he was surgically treated and was treated with internal fixation of plate and screw on 14.04.2010.

During the course of treatment in the hospital the surgical wound got infected NC: 2023:KHC:37693 and the same was treated with higher antibiotics and nutrition and dressing was suggested for every alternate day.
At the time of the discharge he was advised non- weight bearing for six months and dressing for every alternate day.
Accordingly he had taken treatment after discharge.
The Doctor also mentioned about the autopsy that was conducted and reported that the death is due to respiratory failure secondary to sepsis.

After several questions that were put to the Doctor whether the deceased was having other ailments and as there was no nexus between the injury and death, the Doctor had denied the same and nothing was contra elicited from the doctor.
8.

In this case immediately after the accident the deceased was taken to the Pooja Hospital, there he had mentioned about the road traffic accident and thereafter a complaint was given without mentioning the date of the complaint which is not fatal to the case and the police NC:
2023:KHC:37693 have registered complaint on 14.04.2010.
They have conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet.
9. In this kinds of cases it is very difficult to have eye-witnesses.
In this case immediately after the accident the medical records and the police records supports the case of the claimants.
If it is the case of the insurance company that the vehicle is implanted or if there is any contributory negligence on the part of the accused they are supposed to adduce the evidence.
In that regard here in this case they have examined the rider of the vehicle naturally the rider of the vehicle will deny the accident.

Considering the MLC extract, the police records and also the evidence of the Doctor this Court comes to the irresistible conclusion that the accident had taken place because of the negligence on the part of the rider of the vehicle and there is nexus between the injuries and the death as there was an infection to the operated wound and as per the evidence of the doctor every three days the deceased was asked to come to the hospital and change - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:37693 the dressing and as per the post-moterm report also, it says that the respiratory failure secondary to sepsis.
Considering the same this Court is of the view that the court below had rightly awarded the compensation holding the insurance company liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, the appeal of the insurance company is Dismissed.
i) The respondent - insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.
On such deposit, the claimants are is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
